newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska corn behind normal but still good in week.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska corn behind normal but still good in week.

text.p: Cooler temperatures swept Nebraska in the week ended September 15 but corn and soybeans remained in mostly excellent condition, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service weekly update said.
Fall crops remain 10 days to two weeks behind normal.

Corn was rated 26 percent excellent, 56 pct good, 15 pct fair and three pct poor or very poor, about unchanged on a week earlier. The crop advanced to six percent mature from one mature last week and compared to six percent last year and 31 percent on a five-year average.
Corn dented 80 pct vs 55 week ago, 80 year ago, 85 avg.
Harvest of high-moisture corn and seed corn was under way and silage cutting was in full swing, the report said.

Soybeans were rated 23 percent excellent, 54 pct good and 20 pct fair, it said. Statewide, 47 pct had turned color and eight pct dropped leaves, both close to last year but well behind the five-year averages.
Sorghum rated 86 percent good or better, 12 pct fair.
Sorghum mature 2 pct vs nil w/a, 3 y/a, 24 avg.
Sorghum turning color 76 pct vs 45 w/a, 64 y/a, 74 avg.
Wheat planted 25 pct vs 11 w/a, 32 y/a, 36 avg.
Topsoils statewide were rated 81 percent adequate, 18 pct short, and subsoils 83 percent adequate, 16 short.
